questions.question: Define an entrepreneur and explain why entrepreneurs are important to the economy.
questions.expected_answer: An entrepreneur identifies a need or opportunity, comes up with an idea and takes the risk of starting a business, combining natural resources, labour and capital, in the hope of profit. Importance (any): create jobs; produce goods and services; bring innovation; increase competition; pay taxes.

questions.question: Name four characteristics of successful entrepreneurs and explain what a calculated risk is.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: creative/innovative; willing to take calculated risks; determined/hard-working; resilient; self-motivated/initiative; self-confident; responsible; honest; goal-oriented; flexible; leadership. A calculated risk is one that has been thought through, weighing what could go wrong and planning to reduce it.

questions.question: Distinguish between characteristics and skills and name three skills an entrepreneur needs.
questions.expected_answer: Characteristics are personal qualities (who you are); skills are learned abilities (what you can do). Skills (any three): financial (budgets, records, pricing); communication; negotiation; planning and time management; marketing and selling; problem-solving; people/leadership; technical; digital.
